title: America's 'most haunted road' continues to spook travelers
excerpt: The thoroughfare stretches 10 miles, winding through a secluded, uninhabited forest as it connects two small communities near the northern edge of the state.
content:
Phantom headlights, the ghostly figure of a boy who drowned and a 'devil' lurking in the shadows are just a few of the unexplainable phenomena countless travelers have reported on America's 'most haunted road.' 

Clinton Road in New Jersey has been the subject of legend for decades, even before the body of an infamous killer's victim was found there, or satanic markings were found scrawled in the ruins of an early 20th-century estate.

The thoroughfare stretches 10 miles, winding through a secluded, uninhabited forest as it connects two small communities near the northern edge of the state. 

'It has a real kind of isolated, creepy vibe to it,' said Kathy Kelly, a New Jersey based supernatural historian and owner of The Paranormal Museum in Asbury Park.

Kelly, 57, told the Daily Mail that Clinton Road is a 'magnet' for paranormal experiences. She said she has heard stories about it since she was a little girl, and that through her line of work, she hears more stories from recent visitors all the time.

The road runs along Clinton Reservoir, where a turn dubbed Dead Man's Curve that once veered nearly 90 degrees could leave unsuspecting motorists to plummet into frigid waters below.

The sharp corner was realigned into a more modest bend in 2016, but Dead Man's Curve remains home to the ghost of a young boy who drowned after falling off a bridge the turn leads to, according to legend. 

The stories vary, but Kelly told the Daily Mail that she has heard many accounts of people driving down the road and their headlights catching the figure of a boy in the middle of the night. 

Clinton Road in New Jersey is considered to be America's 'Most Haunted Road.' Travelers have reported phantom headlights, the ghost of a boy who drowned and other stories

Some say that the Jersey Devil roams the secluded woods around Clinton Road. A 3d illustration of the cryptid is pictured

Richard Kuklinski, who killed at least five people between 1980 and 1984, dumped the body of one of his victims along Clinton Road

'A lot of the stories are related to the ghost boy, because that's just the creepiest thing on the planet, right?' she said.

Legend says that if you throw a coin from the bridge where the boy fell, it will be tossed back up. Alternative, more gruesome versions say that the apparition will push anyone who looks over the edge of the bridge into the water.

People have also reported phantom cars and headlights that appear out of nowhere on Clinton Road. Kelly said those stories tie into broader folklore 'where if you see one of these cars and you flash the high beams, it's going to come back and get you.'

Then there's the road's connection to the Jersey Devil, an infamous cryptid that has been at the heart of American folklore for centuries. Some say the creature lurks in the remote woods around Clinton Road.

Kelly told the Daily Mail that a lot of people's supernatural experiences on the road could likely be explained by its reputation and visitors coming in with certain expectations. 

But at the same time, 'things did happen there,' the paranormal historian said. 

'One of the Iceman's bodies was found along Clinton Road,' Kelly said. The Iceman was a career criminal named Richard Kuklinski who killed at least five people between 1980 and 1984. 

In 1983, the body of one of his victims, Daniel Deppner, was found on the side of Clinton Road by a cyclist. The body was wrapped in a green garbage bag, and a vulture was pecking at the remains. 

Kathy Kelly, a New Jersey-based supernatural historian and owner of The Paranormal Museum in Asbury Park, told the Daily Mail she has heard stories about Clinton Road since she was a girl

Kuklinski was convicted of murdering Deppner and three others in 1988 and sentenced to life in prison. While incarcerated in 2003, he confessed to killing a New York City detective as well.

Clinton Road also has ties to the Satanic Panic of the 1980s and 90s, as satanic symbols were found inside the ruins of an estate built on the bank of the Clinton Reservoir by a railroad official and banker named Richard James Cross. 

The home, which was constructed to resemble a castle and later dubbed Cross Castle, was built in 1905 for an estimated cost of $1.4 million, equivalent to about $53.6 million today. 

A fire destroyed part of the structure in the mid-20th century, and it fell into ruin. Some believe the ruins then became the site of satanic ritualistic practices.

Local officials razed Cross Castle in 1988, as it was deemed to be an attractive nuisance.

Kelly conceded that satanic symbols were found at the location, and that 'there's a lot of people in New Jersey history that got caught up in ritual and ceremony and did weird stuff.' 

But she said that in all likelihood the symbols in Cross Castle were simply tagged by 'kids blowing off steam.' 

Still, the symbols became yet another piece of lore that contributed to the overall image of Clinton Road, the supernatural historian said. 

Clinton Road is also tied to the Satanic Panic of the 1980s and 90s, as satanic symbols were found in the ruins of a nearby estate called Cross Castle (pictured) built in 1905

'Now you have several generations of people who believed they were Satanists. And so the area has become creepy and scary,' Kelly told the Daily Mail.

'Not because of anything that actually happened there, but because of things that people believed happened there.'

But Kelly also said: 'I think it can be true that something unusual did happen there. People don't really necessarily know what it was, but stories were built up around it.'

Those stories about Clinton Road continue to capture the imagination of people across the country. 

It was officially recognized as America's 'Most Haunted Road' for the third year in a row by the rental car agency SIXT, which determined that more than one million online searches about the road were made over the past year.
